newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: ZAMBIA RELEASES COMMERCIAL BANK CHIEF.
newsitem.headline: ZAMBIA RELEASES COMMERCIAL BANK CHIEF.

text.p: The Zambian government has released the chief executive of the state-owned Zambia National Commercial Bank (ZNCB) , saying he has finished the restructuring job he was hired for.
Finance Minister Ronald Penza told Reuters on Monday that ZNCB managing director Kaitano Chungu had done the job he was asked to do and said the change was not punitive.
"Mr. Chungu is no longer managing director. The period in which he was supposed to restructure the bank is over," Penza said.
"I have appointed his deputy, Samuel Musonda, to act as managing director," he added.
Chungu was recalled from a World Bank project in East Africa to head a planned merger of ZNCB and Meridien BIAO Bank Zambia two years ago.
The government subsequently rescinded its decision to merge the two banks and asked Chungu to lead a restructuring exercise at ZNCB in which over 1,000 jobs were phased out.
Meridien BIAO Bank Zambia, which was faced with severe liquidity problems, was closed down soon after the merger was called off.
